Answer: B
Reason: The serial chest X-rays (Figures 1a, 3a, 4a, 6a) demonstrate a clear progression from initial nodular densities in the middle and lower lung fields to extensive, diffuse bilateral infiltrative involvement with areas of radiolucency (likely representing cystic changes or cavitation), which is characteristic of advanced bronchioloalveolar carcinoma. Options suggesting stability, regression, or isolated upper lobe disease are contradicted by the visible worsening and distribution of opacities over time.
